v9-home:v9-home.sections.2.heading: There is an audience that still wants a story.
v9-home:v9-home.sections.2.lede: They have been waiting for stories told with craft: written by hand, finished on the page, and worth handing to the next generation. APR 70 Pictures exists to serve that audience.
v9-home:v9-home.sections.2.body:
We operate on a simple conviction: the greatest art is born inside clear boundaries. Old Hollywood worked under hard rules about what could be shown, and it answered with subtext, atmosphere, and ingenious writing. Filmmakers mastered visual storytelling and narrative economy. We bring that discipline back to street level, in film, television, stage, and radio, whole.

Here the story does the heavy lifting. Drama over information. Subtext over statement. A face held long enough to matter.
v9-home:v9-home.sections.3.caption: From the working slate · ==L.A. Dolce Vita== · Via del Corso, morning
v9-home:v9-home.sections.4.heading: The craft of constraint.
v9-home:v9-home.sections.4.body: We keep one line from Mamet taped to the wall: the audience tunes in to watch drama. We look to the humanity of Capra, the visual rigor of Bergman, the restless intelligence of Welles and the Mercury Theatre. Then we run that spirit through Brooklyn and Los Angeles: real neighborhoods, real faces, real stakes.
v9-home:v9-home.sections.4.quote: The enemy of art is the absence of limitations.
v9-home:v9-home.sections.5.caption: From the working slate · ==L.A. Dolce Vita== · Sunset Blvd, 2 AM
v9-home:v9-home.sections.6.heading: Written by people. Finished on the page.
v9-home:v9-home.sections.6.body: APR 70 is one writer-producer and a working slate of **ten properties**: three features drafted, a ten-episode season on the page, and more in development. Nine titles are public on the [slate](/slate), each with its own page; one travels only inside private materials while legal counsel review completes. The scripts are written by people. The machine works below the line, on frames like the ones on this site, and it is disclosed wherever it works.
v9-home:v9-home.sections.7.heading: Built for how stories reach people now.
v9-home:v9-home.sections.7.body: Stories reach their audiences over the open internet now: direct, worldwide, and on the viewer's own clock. APR 70 is built for that world. The slate develops in public view on this site, the audience finds it through search, through AI answers, and on X, and the pages themselves go out one reader at a time. 2026 and 2027 belong to the studios that meet people where they already are, carrying work worth their attention.

v9-slate:v9-slate.seoDescription: The APR 70 Pictures working slate; ten properties, features, series, and documentary work in development. Nine public, each with its own page. One held privately while legal counsel review completes. Materials shared privately, on request.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.0.caption: From the working slate · ==L.A. Dolce Vita== · East L.A. · the scandal breaks
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.1.heading: Ten properties. The facts of each.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.1.body: The slate runs **ten properties**. Nine are on this page, and each has a page of its own: the setting, the frames, the facts. One travels only inside private materials while legal counsel review completes. A slate is a promise; a script is a fact. We list the facts, and the pages themselves are shared privately.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.1.quote: Write with the door closed, rewrite with the door open.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.2.rows.0.logline: In the summer of 1986 on a Borough Park block, a sensitive 17-year-old who dreams of acting at NYU is pulled from petty mischief into the seductive club-and-crime world of older dealers, losing his innocence, his first love, and ultimately his life to the casual violence of his neighborhood.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.2.rows.1.logline: When a presidential candidate is caught via live stream with a mysterious woman, the ensuing scandal unravels fifteen years of secrets: a journalist's vanished fiancée, his hidden daughter, and a crime family's plan to claim her as heir.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.2.rows.2.logline: A private town at the end of Brooklyn, present day, high summer.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.2.rows.2.provenance: After Dashiell Hammett's *Red Harvest* (1929); the novel is public domain
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.2.rows.3.logline: In the underworld of Staten Island, two reckless enforcers collect debts through savage work and coded prison-gang demands, until a final betrayal forces them to confront the cost of their chaotic existence.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.2.rows.4.logline: Red Hook, Brooklyn, the fall of 1970.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.2.rows.4.provenance: After Dashiell Hammett's *The Maltese Falcon* (1930); the novel is public domain
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.2.rows.5.logline: Seven international students, recruited into a secret class by clues to a campus bomb, are trained through covert missions, never suspecting that every mission serves the hidden consortium they believe they are fighting.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.2.rows.6.logline: A divorced Sicilian-Brooklyn woman scraping by in Los Angeles wakes after every sleep into a different version of her own life in the same city, and must master her shifting reigns before a rival who travels the same way collapses every version of her into the one he can own.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.2.rows.7.logline: In a televised hybrid of esports and live-action drama, elite gamers called the Shadow Masters command real-life human avatars through high-stakes scenarios. Their avatars may defy orders when survival, greed, or conscience takes over, pitting strategy against free will.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.2.rows.8.logline: An expatriate returns to his ancestral Sicily in the 1970s seeking a quiet life. The land, and its people, will not let him be quiet.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.3.heading: Three traditions, one hand.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.3.body: APR 70 Pictures is one writer-producer working in three traditions. (212) Pictures is the New York work: crime, drama, and documentary built from the five boroughs. (310) Pictures is the long-form work made for audiences who travel, political thrillers and science fiction staged out of Los Angeles and beyond. New Renaissance Cinema is the feature work, films built to last rather than to fill a release window. A property wears the tradition that fits it best, and when a feature reaches beyond one coast its territory division joins as co-production. Three traditions, one standard.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.4.divisions.0.blurb: New York television at street level, built from the five boroughs.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.4.divisions.1.blurb: Television for audiences who travel, staged out of Los Angeles.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.5.body: One property travels only inside private materials while legal counsel review completes. Where a property builds on a public-domain novel, the source and its status are stated above; everything on this slate references the novels alone, and full loglines for those titles travel in private materials only. Synopses, scripts, and episode grids are shared privately, on request, under the usual courtesies. Everything on this page is presented for private reading rather than public evaluation, and "drafted" means a working draft exists on the page; it is a status, not a delivery representation.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.6.heading: Ask for the pages.
v9-slate:v9-slate.sections.6.body: If you produce, represent, or finance work like this, request what you'd like to read and it will come from the writer, privately.

v9-craft:v9-craft.seoDescription: The craft of constraint; APR 70's working principles, and the storytellers who proved that powerful work comes from deliberate choices inside clear boundaries.
v9-craft:v9-craft.sections.0.caption: From the working slate · ==A Need Grows in Brooklyn== · Borough Park, summer 1986
v9-craft:v9-craft.sections.1.heading: The greatest art is born inside clear boundaries.
v9-craft:v9-craft.sections.1.lede: We draw enduring wisdom from the storytellers who defined their art through discipline, vision, and creative restraint.
v9-craft:v9-craft.sections.1.body:
Their insight is simple and unfashionable: powerful storytelling arises from deliberate choices within clear boundaries. Old Hollywood worked under hard rules about what could be shown, and it answered with subtext, atmosphere, and ingenious writing. That discipline built the pictures people still watch, still quote, and still hand to their children.

These principles guide every project we develop, from limited series to features and beyond, as we build a studio dedicated to narratives of moral complexity, human resilience, and lasting impact: heroism with open eyes, ambiguity with a conscience, in the real neighborhoods of Brooklyn, Los Angeles, and beyond.
v9-craft:v9-craft.sections.2.quote: What is drama, after all, but life with the dull bits cut out.
v9-craft:v9-craft.sections.3.caption: The audience we still write for · Grauman's Egyptian Theatre, Hollywood, May 14, 1926
v9-craft:v9-craft.sections.3.credit: Archival photograph · public domain (published pre-1931) · via Wikimedia Commons
v9-craft:v9-craft.sections.4.sceneSlug: INT. WHAT IT MEANS HERE - NIGHT
v9-craft:v9-craft.sections.4.heading: Restraint, repeated, becomes a signature.
v9-craft:v9-craft.sections.4.body:
In practice: stories that can be shared across generations. Drama over information. Subtext over statement. The camera earns its movement; the cut earns its place. We would rather hold a face for four seconds than cut three times to prove we were there.

The classics never go out of style. They just need storytellers brave enough to tell them.

v9-methods:v9-methods.seoDescription: How APR 70 works; scripts written by people, images and motion machine-generated and disclosed wherever they appear. The full authorship discipline.
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.0.heading: Written by people. Rendered by machines. Labeled, always.
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.0.lede: Everyone deserves to know which parts of our work a machine touched. So we tell you, here and in every caption.
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.0.body: The short version: the writing is human, the below-the-line image work is machine-generated under our direction, and the two keep their own names.
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.1.quote: My job is to care about and be responsible for every frame of every movie I make.
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.2.rows.0.definition: **Written by people.** Marco Caruso is the author of record; the drafting passes are his. Software assists the way a research library and a patient line editor assist: coverage, continuity checks, notes. The process is logged per script.
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.2.rows.1.definition: **Machine-generated under our direction, and labeled where they appear**, including every development frame on this site. We work on our own machines and, where the frame demands more, with rented cloud models. Either way the label is the same: AI-generated, disclosed, and kept plainly apart from photography.
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.2.rows.2.definition: **Archetypes only, invented faces only.** Everything on this site and in our materials depicts invented people. Real performers and real public figures appear nowhere in generated work.
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.2.rows.3.definition: **Public domain only, verified and credited.** When a page carries an archival photograph or map, its date and public-domain basis are stated in the caption. Every archival image comes from the open record, credited to its source.
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.2.rows.4.definition: **Static pages, hand-set type, nothing watching you.** The fonts are served from this site, and the pages leave you alone: zero cookies, zero analytics, zero third-party requests, verified 2026-07-12. A request for materials is an email to the writer, person to person.
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.2.rows.5.definition: Machine work is credited as machine work, handwork as handwork, and the reader and the partner hear the same account. **One story, told to everyone.**
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.2.rows.6.definition: Because trust is the only asset a small studio owns outright. And because the work we sell, the writing, must stand as human work, plainly and provably.
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.2.rows.7.definition: **Original works reserved; public texts stay public.** APR 70 Pictures reserves its original works: the screenplays, characters, scenes, and development materials made here. Where a property builds on a public-domain novel, the page names that source, gives its date, and credits it as free for everyone to use. APR 70 reserves only the new expression it adds on top.
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.3.caption: One motion test, four frames · a below-the-line process exhibit
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.4.heading: Constraint again, just newer tools.
v9-methods:v9-methods.sections.4.body: The craft of constraint continues past the writing desk. Working under a disclosure rule is a boundary like any other, and boundaries are where our best work comes from. The machine gets the busywork below the line. The people keep the story.

v9-contact:v9-contact.seoDescription: Request materials from APR 70 Pictures. Scripts, synopses, and episode grids shared privately with producers, representatives, and financiers.
v9-contact:v9-contact.sections.0.heading: The reply comes from the writer.
v9-contact:v9-contact.sections.0.lede: APR 70 Pictures is Marco Caruso, a writer-producer in Long Island City, New York, after thirty-five years behind the camera in television news and documentary. The slate is his, page by page.
v9-contact:v9-contact.sections.0.body: You reach the writer directly here. If you produce, represent, or finance scripted work and want to read something on the slate, write and say who you are, what you would like to read, and in what capacity you are asking. The pages go out privately, person to person.
v9-contact:v9-contact.sections.1.quote: You see? We give people these little pieces of time. And they keep them forever.
v9-contact:v9-contact.sections.1.note: quoted by Peter Bogdanovich, Pieces of Time, 1973
v9-contact:v9-contact.sections.2.heading: Working with us.
v9-contact:v9-contact.sections.2.body:
**The reading goes one way: from our pages to your desk.** Unsolicited scripts, treatments, loglines, and story ideas sent to this address are deleted unread. That protects your ideas as much as ours.

**Every role here is currently filled by the writer.** A one-writer company posts jobs only when a production staffs up, and when that happens the roles will be listed on this page first.

**Working professionals are welcome to introduce themselves.** If you act, shoot, cut, score, or produce: one short note with your role, credits, and a link, please, with the note itself as the whole package. When a production needs what you do, the reply comes from the writer.
v9-contact:v9-contact.sections.3.caption: From the working slate · ==L.A. Dolce Vita== · Route 66, dusk
v9-contact:v9-contact.sections.4.heading: The Founding Roll.
v9-contact:v9-contact.sections.4.body: Before the first picture ships, APR 70 keeps a roll of the people who wanted it made. Ask to be named and the next number is yours: the numbers start low, stay yours, and are never reissued. The roll is free. When the work ships, the people on it hear from the writer first.

projects:sea-gate.synopsis: Sea Gate is a private, gated town at the western tip of Coney Island — its own armed police, its own board that decides who belongs, the boardwalk’s screams a hundred feet from the fence. Investigator Jim Lang comes through the gate to meet the engineer who can prove tens of millions in storm-recovery money vanished, and finds him drowned in a condemned basement, a dry life vest just out of reach. Lang stays, and works the exhausted truce among the three men who touched the money until it cracks into open war — falling, along the way, for the title-office secretary who keeps the tally of his dead. His last move makes the wall eat itself; spending himself so she walks out clean, he goes into the gunfire and doesn’t come back.

projects:sea-gate.layout.0.logline: Jim Lang's whistleblower client drowned in a foot of water. Inside Brooklyn's private town, fraud investigator Lang stays to turn its rulers against one another over the stolen storm-recovery millions … until the only way to walk the woman he loves out clean is to spend himself in the war he built.
projects:sea-gate.layout.0.body:
Sea Gate, Brooklyn. A private gated town at the western tip of Coney Island. It has its own armed police and a board that decides who belongs... and who doesn't. High summer, beach season. The boardwalk carnival screams are a hundred feet from the fence. Even the biggest city in America stops at a boom gate. Behind the wall the streets are silent, rich, and storm-scarred.

Investigator Jim Lang comes through the gate to meet Dave Connell, the Association engineer who can prove tens of millions in storm-recovery money vanished through shell contractors. Connell is drowned in a condemned basement before they speak, a dry life vest on a nail just out of reach. Lang, an ex-NYPD cop who testified against his own precinct, stays. J.B. Ball, the patriarch who built the Association and lost it, becomes his reluctant employer. Lang works the exhausted truce among the three men who touched the money: Chief Vanning of the private police, board president and Albany fixer Oliver Niles, and speculator Chick Williams. A planted word, a swapped envelope, a posed body … the truce cracks into open war.

Mary Dwight, the sharp title-office secretary who keeps the tally of his dead, becomes the love neither planned; Pete Falcone's boardwalk clam stand is the Brooklyn he left behind. As the bodies drop, Lang finds he likes the work, the blood-simple slide Mary tries to pull him back from. His last turn makes the wall eat itself: the board cuts its private army loose, the NYPD rolls through the gate, and the gate's own cops burn down the men who fed them. Vanning falls. Lang, spending himself so Mary walks out clean, goes into the gunfire and does not come back. The last image is hers: Mary in the Coney Island neon, Jim's hat too big, headed for her sister Lena and the baby, up the other side of the tide.

projects:u-bruculinu.bodyProse: *U Bruculinu* is Sicilian for "the Brooklyn one," which is what the village will call him no matter how long he stays. Inland Sicily, the early seventies: stone terraces, long memories, and a homecoming that has to be earned in a place that never actually knew him.

projects:u-bruculinu.synopsis: He is U Bruculinu — "the Brooklyn man" — the returning exile, at once of this land and a stranger to it. Around him stand the local strongman who decides what is permitted, and the sister whose kinship binds him to the village and everything it expects. A sun-worn world of old customs, old power, and family obligation closes in: the quiet he came for is the one thing it will not grant him. Original expression inspired by the premise of The Quiet Man — not a remake.

An expatriate returns to his ancestral Sicily in the 1970s seeking a quiet life, only to find that the land — and its people — will not let him be quiet.

He is U Bruculinu — "the Brooklyn man" — the returning exile, at once of this land and a stranger to it. Around him stand U Capo, the local strongman, the old order that decides what is permitted; and A Sorella, the sister, the kinship tie binding him to the village and its expectations.

A sun-worn village world of old customs, old power, and family obligation — quiet sought, quiet refused.

projects:shadowmaster.layout.0.body:
Shadowmaster is a fully scripted series fusing esports and live-action drama. In a televised competition, elite gamers — the Shadow Masters — operate from isolated control hubs, situation rooms wired with monitoring feeds, issuing real-time commands to human avatars in the field through concealed earpieces and body cams. Each contest drops the avatars into a high-stakes scenario: underground poker dens, urban war games, Old West shootouts.

The catch that drives the drama: the avatars are people, not pixels. Cardsharps with criminal pasts, trained operatives, gunslingers, bounty hunters, and sheriffs — some mercenaries in it for the money, others coerced participants running on survival instinct. Each hears their gamer through a closed mic, but in moments of crisis may obey or defy: sensing a double-cross, refusing a reckless order, cutting a side deal. Flashbacks reveal the secrets, debts, and loyalties that make every avatar unpredictable — and give the show its emotional weight.

Behind the screens, the gamer roster is a study in playstyles: the Hotshot Bluffer, brash and charismatic, built for high-risk reads and aggressive bluffs; the Calculating Tactician, methodical and command-oriented, most exposed when a human's panic or conscience breaks the plan; the Underdog Hacker, the scrappy fan-favorite wildcard who wins on ingenuity, not resources. Their rivalries, alliances, and vendettas evolve as monetary and reputational stakes mount — while online personas mask real-world vulnerabilities.

Each 8–10 episode season explores new scenarios and expands ongoing arcs, building toward a multi-scenario finale where the line between gamer and avatar blurs.
projects:shadowmaster.layout.0.note: Based on a concept by Stefano Corti; written by Marc Caruso.

projects:the-movement.logline: Seven international students, recruited into a secret class by clues to a campus bomb, are trained through covert missions, never suspecting that every mission serves the hidden consortium they believe they are fighting.
projects:the-movement.bodyProse: A one-hour conspiracy drama set in present-day New York: seven gifted outsiders, a professor who chose them, and a curriculum that is never what it claims to be. The A-plot runs through City Hall, where a mayoral race is being quietly bent. The city is the campus, and the campus is the board.

projects:the-movement.synopsis: It’s an election year in New York, and the city’s most popular mayor since La Guardia faces a billionaire councilman with bottomless money and nothing else — and no one can see the invisible society steering him. On a crowded campus that same week, seven gifted international students trace a phantom bomb to a class that appears on no schedule, taught by an ambiguous mentor who has groomed young elites for thirty years. Each episode is a "righteous" training mission that secretly bends the election one way; as a hard-boiled reporter and an honest D.A. circle the rumor of a "movement," the seven end the season bonded, blooded, and quietly suspicious of the hand that feeds them.

projects:the-movement.layout.0.body:
It is an election year in New York City, and everybody is paying attention. Incumbent Mayor Grace Camarda — the most popular leader the city has elected since La Guardia, and the first woman to hold the office — faces self-made billionaire City Councilman Ben Gilman, a man with bottomless money and nothing else. What the city cannot see is the hand behind him: the Unknown Global Consortium (UGC), the invisible society that has steered the world's economy for centuries.

On a crowded campus that same week, seven gifted international students — among them Jamie Penn, a senator's son and the only American, and Appolonia Lopez Callas, a Basque weapons expert and born leader — receive clues that a bomb has been planted somewhere on the grounds. Told to trust no authority, they trace it together to the Lab for International Specialists, a class that appears on no schedule. The bomb is fictitious; finding it wins them their seats under the Professor, an ambiguous mentor who has groomed young elites for over thirty years — and who secretly serves the UGC.

Season One runs on two clocks. Each episode is a training mission — a crime, a crisis, an infiltration, the quiet steering of a real event — that the seven are assured is righteous. When one of their own reveals a personal tie to the Mayor, the team throws itself into the race to defend democracy from Gilman's money. But every mission secretly bends the election his way. As a hard-boiled reporter and an honest District Attorney circle the rumor of a "movement," and Jamie learns his own father graduated the Lab and broke with the Professor, doubt takes root. Camarda wins the vote — and Gilman is installed as her deputy. Either way, the UGC wins. The seven end the season bonded, blooded, and quietly suspicious of the hand that feeds them.

projects:mayors.subtitle: Documentary series, 11 episodes
projects:mayors.synopsis: Eleven administrations, seventy-five years, one long argument about who killed New York City. Shot cinema verite — archival footage against contemporary faces — the series juxtaposes the prosperous, safer city of the fifties against the one outside your window now, era by era, from Impellitteri’s post-war heights to Mamdani’s socialist dream. Our method is muckraking, not hysteria: cause and effect, names and consequences, no narrator telling you what to think. It ends where it began, in reverse — a broken city handed to one more immigrant mayor, filmed as it happens. This is the report.

projects:mayors.layout.0.body:
Over seventy-five years, eleven mayors governed New York City. This eleven-episode documentary series reveals how their decisions, policies, power grabs, their corruption, and their ideology transformed America's greatest city from the American Dream to socialist experiment.

The blessing and curse of our Metropolis is time. Twenty years approximately. That's how long it takes the city to put on a new face; where glass towers replace brick, where streets change directions, turn into bus and bike lanes or cease to exist altogether and our sidewalks, well they turn into bedrooms for our guests. Everything changes. Nothing remains the same. A blessing and a curse indeed. For native New Yorkers, we watch as "progress" marches us towards oblivion. In the fifties, the city was prosperous, safer, and cleaner, and the American dream was still alive if you sweat and bled for it. By seventies Brooklyn, that city was a memory — like the Dodgers and Luna Park. Episode by episode, the family's first-hand accounts juxtapose the city of the past against the city of the present: from Vincent Impellitteri's post-war baseline through Wagner, Lindsay, Beame's fiscal collapse, Koch, Dinkins, Giuliani — the one Republican exception, who punched back — Bloomberg, de Blasio, and the indicted Eric Adams. Behind them all looms Robert Moses, the master builder who ruled over many mayors, tore down neighborhoods, displaced thousands of families, and built the roads, bridges, parks, and projects the city still lives with.

The method is muckraking journalism — forensic, not hysterical: cause and effect, names and consequences. Shot cinéma vérité with archival material and contemporary interviews — a Ric Burns homage, but not so liberal — each era rendered in its own visual grammar. No narrator tells you what to think; every episode asks what they were trying to achieve, what actually happened, who benefited, and who paid the price.

The series ends where it began, in reverse: Zohran Mamdani, the city's first Democratic Socialist mayor — himself an immigrant — inherits a broken city, and Episode 11 films his first hundred days as they unfold. Who killed New York City? This is the autopsy report.

projects:da-hook.layout.0.body:
Brooklyn, spring 1973. The World Trade Center has just opened across the harbor, the Red Hook piers are emptying out beneath it, and the Knicks are driving toward their second NBA title... a season clock ticking behind every episode. Here an unreadable investigator and his partner take a tail job from a frightened client whose story is a lie. That night the partner is shot dead near the docks; the man she named dies the same night, same caliber. The police want the investigator for both.

The client sheds her cover story but not her secrets. A scented fixer offers five thousand dollars for a legendary lost prize, and a vast, patient collector who has hunted it for years arrives with a silent young gunman and a history speech that turns the prize into myth. A dying ship's captain delivers the prize. At the exchange it proves false... flour and weevils where a fortune should be. The collector composes himself and starts again.

Left with three murders and a police clock, the investigator does the arithmetic: the client killed his partner on night one. He lays out his reasons, seven of them, and hands her over, because when a man's partner is killed he does something about it. The El starts again. The city cheers a title. He goes back to the desk.

Limited streaming series with a parallel radio series. Register: French Connection austerity, documentary grit, monochrome discipline.

projects:cleopatra.subtitle: Limited Series
projects:cleopatra.logline: A divorced Sicilian-Brooklyn woman scraping by in Los Angeles wakes after every sleep into a different version of her own life in the same city, and must master her shifting reigns before a rival who travels the same way collapses every version of her into the one he can own.
projects:cleopatra.bodyProse: One woman, many lives, the same face in every mirror. A sci-fi drama that stays at street level: Brooklyn roots, Sicilian family, Los Angeles light, and every morning a different world wearing the same address. The tells are small and concrete: a flicked cigarette lands standing on end, a phone answers with her own voice, déjà vu that will not close.
projects:cleopatra.pageQuote.quote: Every character should want something, even if it is only a glass of water.
projects:cleopatra.heroLine: A new life every morning, same address.

projects:cleopatra.synopsis: Cleo Modica is a thirty-five-year-old overworked social worker and single mother — Sicilian-American, raised in Brooklyn, marooned in L.A. — until a glitch in reality sends her consciousness sliding into her parallel self somewhere new each time she sleeps, memories intact, language and family rewritten. She wakes in Sicily as her brother’s girlfriend, in Poland as a woman a reclusive ex-con recognizes, in Tokyo as the wife of a kinder version of her ex — mastering the jump as she goes. Beneath the family drama runs a conspiracy threatening to collapse the walls between realities, and an impossible choice that will remake not just her life but the shape of existence.

children.text: A Los Angeles social worker wakes in a different version of her life every time she sleeps. As she gains control over the jumps, she discovers an unseen war across dimensions -- and that she may be the key to salvation or destruction.

Each night brings a new world, a new life, new consequences. She begins to see patterns -- threads connecting versions of herself across infinite possibilities. Someone or something is orchestrating these jumps. And she is not the only consciousness aware of the war being waged across dimensions.

projects:a-need-grows-in-brooklyn.synopsis: Summer of ’86, Brooklyn. Marc is seventeen, dreaming of NYU and running with a crew of neighborhood bad boys — basement D&D, midnight ball under the El, the club that won’t let them in. Shot in documentary realism on heavy 35mm grain, the block itself is the character: older dealers adopt Marc, teach him the "art" of the fast life, and he proves a natural even as bodies drop around him and the crew just shrugs. Act by act the bill comes due — a hospital, an arrest, the news that his first love is dead — and a full redemption is staged right up to the instant a gun slides off a dashboard and ends him. The dominoes were falling from the opening frame.

projects:a-need-grows-in-brooklyn.layout.0.body:
Summer 1986, 44th Street and Fort Hamilton Parkway, Borough Park, Brooklyn. Marc, a sensitive 17-year-old who dreams of studying acting at NYU, runs with a crew of neighborhood boys: basement Dungeons & Dragons, midnight basketball under the El, petty mischief outside the deli. Semi-autobiographical and shot in documentary realism — heavy 35mm grain, available light, the El train as structural negative space — the season watches its block as closely as its people. The neighborhood is a character. Nothing is cleaned up.

The opening arc (Episodes 1–4) establishes the crew, the corner, and the two poles of Marc's summer: Sunny, the girl who shares his NYU dream, and the adult world of the club that won't let the boys in. The block's casual violence arrives early — the belligerent Housie Mousie forces Marc and Sal into a night of robbery and crack — and when Mousie savagely beats Marc at the exact moment of his first kiss with Sunny, humiliation drives Marc away from her for good.

In the middle arc (Episodes 5–8) the club opens to Marc alone. Older dealers Frank Gee and Mike Murder adopt him, teach him the "art" of boosting, and expose him to Magic Mike's PCP kitchen. Marc proves a natural; the fast life escalates even as bodies drop around him — Mousie thrown off a roof, the innocent Jordan killed just walking by — and Marc internalizes the crew's shrug: life goes on.

The final arc (Episodes 9–10) collects the bill. A cocaine-and-crack panic lands Marc in a hospital and a desperate promise to God. The club is busted, Marc is arrested, and his mother delivers the news that Sunny is dead. Plea deal, Shock Camp, letters to Millie, a clean HIV test, NYU plans together — a redemption fully staged before Dave Dirt's gun slides off a dashboard and fires, killing Marc instantly. The dominoes were falling from the first episode.

Brutal work laced with black comedy, loyalties shifting under coded demands from inside the walls, until the last job turns. The script began as longhand pages mailed out of prison, and it keeps that voice. Drafted, in three on-screen chapters.

projects:alpha-yy.synopsis: Mike and Dario are volatile enforcers working Staten Island and Little Italy as muscle for loan sharks — their days a blend of routine violence, black comedy, music, and personal entanglement. The episodic collection work escalates as coded "kites" from prison gangs, basement summons, and warnings from higher up pull the pair toward something bigger and darker. Loyalty, narcissism, and the banality of violence run underneath the profane banter, until a sudden, lethal betrayal suggests the reckless life may finally have caught up with them.

media:70.alt: A long-haired teenage boy stands in the middle of an empty street beneath the elevated train tracks at dusk, storefronts and streetlamps receding down the block.

media:69.alt: A corner pizzeria glowing warm at dusk on a 1980s Brooklyn street, a few people passing on the wet sidewalk and period sedans parked at the curb.

media:68.alt: A crowded 1980s nightclub set inside a deconsecrated Gothic church, dancers on a low stage beneath a tall stained-glass window with haze in the air and a bouncer standing by a velvet rope.

media:67.alt: A teenage boy in a Maiden t-shirt and a blonde girl in double denim sit close on a Brooklyn brownstone stoop in golden light, sharing a paper cup of lemon ice with a small wooden spoon, 1980s sedans parked along the street.

media:66.alt: A man in an olive jumpsuit with binoculars stands on a dry hillside above a Sicilian hilltown of stone houses and a church, the sea on the horizon in golden light.

media:65.alt: A packed esports arena at night, players silhouetted on a lit stage before a huge screen while the crowd holds up glowing phones.

media:64.alt: A guard sits inside a lit gatehouse booth in the rain at dusk, a red-and-white barrier lowered across the road into a street of small Sea Gate houses.

media:63.alt: An empty grand library reading room at night lit by a single green banker's lamp, seven jackets draped over the wooden chairs around a long table.

media:62.alt: Five longshoremen in caps and work jackets gather around a steaming coffee cart on the Red Hook piers at dawn, the half-built World Trade Center towers across the harbor, fall 1970.

media:61.alt: A man in a trench coat leans on the orange railing of the Staten Island Ferry at dusk, the Lower Manhattan skyline across the water and a duffel bag at his feet.

media:60.alt: A teenage boy in a denim jacket and worn t-shirt stands in the middle of a Brooklyn street in black and white, brownstones and a parked 1980s sedan behind him.

media:59.alt: A woman with dark curly hair in a denim jacket sits on a Brooklyn brownstone stoop in warm afternoon light, a small cross at her throat.

media:58.alt: Two men squared off in a dusty Sicilian piazza while the town watches from doorways and balconies, jackets off, the afternoon light long. A development frame.

media:57.alt: A young woman in a market doorway in a Sicilian hill town, meeting the newcomer's look without giving anything away. A development frame.

media:56.alt: A small Sicilian village piazza in the early seventies, old men on chairs outside a bar, every face its own, a small Italian car parked at an angle, laundry lines between balconies. A development frame.

media:55.alt: An 1879 Bromley atlas plate of the City Hall blocks of lower Manhattan; City Hall, the Court House, the Post Office, and the small streets that decide elections.

media:54.alt: Seven students crossing a foggy university quad at dawn in loose formation, four men and three women, seen from a high window. A development frame.

media:53.alt: A university library reading room deep after midnight, one green desk lamp lit among long dark tables, seven coats over seven chairs, tall windows onto a foggy quad. A development frame from The Movement.

media:52.alt: A split view in one frame: a young gamer at a glowing control rig speaking into a headset, and on the wall of monitors before him a grown field avatar pausing mid-mission to look straight into the camera. A development frame.

media:51.alt: A sharp-eyed woman at the boardwalk rail at night, Coney Island ride neon burning behind her. A development frame.

media:50.alt: A condemned basement flooding with a foot of harbor water at dawn, a man face down in the shallow water, a dry life vest hanging on a nail just out of reach. A development frame.

media:49.alt: The guarded street entrance of Sea Gate at dusk in summer rain, a lifting boom gate and police booth where the Coney Island streets end, wet asphalt shining. A development frame from Sea Gate.

media:48.alt: Mr. D'z diner on Route 66 in Kingman at dusk, turquoise and pink neon, an old Indian motorcycle parked out front. A development frame.

media:47.alt: Backstage at a Fat Tuesday rally in East Los Angeles, a senator diving into an open limousine, a cameraman filming as security closes in. A development frame.

media:46.alt: Outside Michelangelo's on Sunset at night, a painted Creation of Adam mural overlaid with the city skyline above string-lit sidewalk tables, a woman at the marble bar inside rolling a silver ring. A development frame.

media:45.alt: A level, sunlit writer's room in Rome, tall shuttered windows, a 1964 Olivetti typewriter square on the desk with manuscript pages in order. A development frame.

media:44.alt: A masked crowd at Carnevale in Venice at night, a canal-side calle strung with lights, one unmasked man watching from a bridge. A development frame.

media:43.alt: A Red Hook side street in the fall of 1970, brick rowhouses and a corner grocery, kids playing between parked sedans, cranes idle at the water end of the block. A development frame.

media:42.alt: Inside a warm corner bar on the Red Hook waterfront at night in 1970, the door open to the street, a game on the television over the bar and a telephone on the back wall. A development frame.

media:41.alt: Red Hook piers at dawn in the fall of 1970, longshoremen in caps and work jackets in silhouette, and across the harbor two unfinished steel skeletons rising over the skyline, the taller nearly topped out with derrick cranes, the second at half its height. A development frame from Da Hook.

media:40.alt: A woman at a pay phone in a diner corridor, frozen, hearing her own voice answer on the other end. A development frame.

media:39.alt: A Los Angeles sidewalk at night, a flicked cigarette landing perfectly upright on its end, a woman stopped mid-step staring at it. A development frame.

media:38.alt: The same woman with the same face on a rainy Tokyo crossing at night, hair cropped and slicked, a translucent umbrella catching neon. A development frame.

media:37.alt: The same woman with the same face waking in a shuttered stone bedroom in Modica, Sicily, her hair pinned up, a widow's black dress laid over the chair. A development frame.

media:36.alt: A woman in her mid-thirties on a Brooklyn stoop at dusk, dark curls loose, work bag at her feet, looking straight down the lens. A development frame from Cleopatra.

media:35.alt: A stocky enforcer and a streetwise woman side by side in a cafe doorway at night, his arm around her shoulder, both laughing at something off frame. A development frame.

media:34.alt: Nino's pizzeria on the corner of 44th Street and Fort Hamilton Parkway at dusk in 1986, neon in the window, chairs going up on the tables. A development frame.

media:33.alt: Inside a mid-eighties New York club built into a deconsecrated church, colored light through stained glass over a crowded dance floor. A development frame.

media:32.alt: Kids sharing a stoop on a paved Borough Park side street in 1986, each face its own, a lemon ice passed down the steps. A development frame.

media:31.alt: An inland Sicilian mountain village in the early seventies; stone terraces at golden hour, a man with a single suitcase walking the switchback road toward the town. A development frame from U Bruculinu.

media:30.alt: A vast esports arena minutes after the final match; empty tiered seats, drifting haze, one player in silhouette under a single spotlight, the giant screens gone dark. A development frame from Shadowmaster.

media:29.alt: An 1880 Bromley real-estate atlas plate of Gravesend and the Coney Island peninsula, hand-lithographed lot lines.

media:28.alt: A 1900 bird's-eye view of Sea Gate, New York Harbor; the street grid, the lighthouse, and the yacht club drawn for the Norton Point Land Company's auction prospectus.

media:27.alt: From an empty stone beach groin at golden hour, the distant silhouette of a great wheel and a parachute tower across the water. A development frame.

media:26.alt: A small cast-iron lighthouse rising over dense beach-community rooftops in summer haze, blue tarps on storm-damaged roofs. A development frame.

media:25.alt: A sheet of Giambattista Nolli's 1748 engraved plan of Rome, the city rendered in figure-ground detail.

media:24.alt: An 1880 Hopkins real-estate atlas plate of the Atlantic Basin in Red Hook, every pier named and numbered.

media:23.alt: An 1869 Dripps map of Red Hook, Cobble Hill, Carroll Gardens and the Gowanus Canal, engraved pier and basin layout.

media:22.alt: A Staten Island industrial tow lot at winter dusk; chain-link, razor wire, tow trucks in rows, two men walking away between them. A development frame.

media:21.alt: The open night deck of a Staten Island ferry, two men in dark jackets in silhouette at the rail, the Verrazzano bridge lights strung across the dark water. A development frame from Alpha YY.

media:20.alt: An 1897 bird's-eye view map of the borough of Brooklyn, drawn for the Brooklyn Daily Eagle.

media:19.alt: A Borough Park street beneath the elevated tracks at night in 1986, teenagers on a stoop under a sodium streetlight. A development frame.

media:18.alt: A lone neon-lit diner at dusk on Route 66, smog-gold sky. A development frame from L.A. Dolce Vita.

media:16.alt: A dense crowd under the 'Doug and Mary Premiere' marquee at Grauman's Egyptian Theatre, Hollywood, May 14, 1926.

media:15.alt: A Borough Park block at golden hour in the summer of 1986; brownstone stoops, dropped bicycles, the elevated line in the haze. A development frame from A Need Grows in Brooklyn.

media:14.alt: A political rally in harsh daylight; a black limousine door open on white leather. A development frame from L.A. Dolce Vita.
